skill.name: clojure-review
skill.description: Review Clojure and ClojureScript code changes for Metabase style, module, API, database, driver, test, and readability conventions.
skill.summary: Metabase-focused Clojure review checklist for style, tests, APIs, modules, and database conventions.
skill.author: metabase

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code spans and Clojure style examples. I confirmed the findings that correspond to documented ./bin/mage lint, format, test, readability, and REPL commands; they are legitimate Metabase workflows but execute repository-local tooling.

remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before running ./bin/mage commands, and run them only in trusted Metabase workspaces.
Prefer clojure-mcp tools when available, and limit REPL code to reviewer-controlled expressions.

remediation.issue: Markdown command examples trigger static detections
remediation.suggestion: Keep command examples clearly framed as optional developer actions, not automatic skill behavior.

static_findings.snippet: This guide covers Clojure and ClojureScript coding conventions for Metabase. See also: `CLOJURE_STYL
- Acceptable abbreviations: `acc`, `i`, `pred`, `coll`, `n`, `s`, `k`, `f`
- Use `kebab-case` for all variables, functions, and constants
- Pure functions should be nouns describing the value they return (e.g., `age` not `calculate-age` o
- Functions with side effects must end with `!`
- Map destructuring should use kebab-case local bindings even if the map uses `snake_case` keys
- Every public var in `src` or `enterprise/backend/src` must have docstring
- Reference other vars with `[[other-var]]` not backticks
- `TODO` format: `;; TODO (Name M/D/YY) -- description`
- Make everything `^:private` unless it is used elsewhere
- Try to organize namespaces to avoid `declare` (put public functions near the end)
- No blank lines within definition forms (except pairwise `let`/`cond`)
- Prefer namespaced keywords for internal use: `:query-type/normal` not `:normal`
- Tag variables with `:arglists` metadata if they're functions but wouldn't otherwise have it
- Break large tests into separate `deftest` forms for logically separate test cases
- Test names should end in `-test` or `-test-<number>`
- Mark pure function tests `^:parallel`
- Follow `metabase.<module>.*` pattern
- Source in `src/metabase/<module>/`
- Follow `metabase-enterprise.<module>.*` pattern
- Source in `enterprise/backend/src/metabase_enterprise/<module>/`
- REST API endpoints go in `<module>.api` or `<module>.api.*` namespaces
- Put module public API in `<module>.core` using Potemkin imports
- Put Toucan models in `<module>.models.*`
- Put settings in `<module>.settings`
- Put schemas in `<module>.schema`
- Do not cheat module linters with `:clj-kondo/ignore [:metabase/modules]`
- All new endpoints must have response schemas (`:- <schema>` after route string)
- Request bodies use `snake_case`
- Routes use singular nouns (e.g., `/api/dashboard/:id`)
- `GET` endpoints should not have side effects (except analytics)
- `defendpoint` forms should be small wrappers around Toucan model code
- No raw MBQL introspection outside of `lib`, `lib-be`, or `query-processor` modules
- Application database uses `snake_case` identifiers
- Use `t2/select-one-fn` instead of fetching entire rows for one column
- New driver multimethods must be mentioned in `docs/developers-guide/driver-changelog.md`
- Driver implementations should pass `driver` argument to other driver multimethods
- Minimize logic inside `read-column-thunk` in JDBC-based drivers
- No `#_:clj-kondo/ignore` (keyword form)
- Use `:internal` `defsetting` instead
- **Lint PR:** `./bin/mage kondo-updated master` (or whatever target branch)
- **Lint File:** `./bin/mage kondo <file or files>`
- **Lint Changes:** `./bin/mage kondo-updated HEAD`
- **Format:** `./bin/mage cljfmt-files [path]`
- **Run a test:** `./bin/mage run-tests namespace/test-name`
- **Run all tests in a namespace:** `./bin/mage run-tests namespace`
- **Run all tests for a module:** `./bin/mage run-tests test/metabase/notification` Because the modu
Note: the `./bin/mage run-tests` command accepts multiple args, so you can pass
`./bin/mage run-tests namespace/test-name namespace/other-test namespace/third-test`
`./bin/mage run-tests test/metabase/module1 test/metabase/module2` to run 2 modules.
- **Check Code Readability:** `./bin/mage -check-readable <file> [line-number]`
> **Note:** If you have `clojure-mcp` tools available (check for tools like `clojure_eval`),
> **always prefer those over `./bin/mage -repl`**. The MCP tools provide better integration,
> richer feedback, and avoid shell escaping issues. Only use `./bin/mage -repl` as a fallback
- **Evaluating Clojure Code:** `./bin/mage -repl '<code>'`
- Send code to the metabase process REPL using: `./bin/mage -repl '(+ 1 1)'` where `(+ 1 1)` is your
- See `./bin/mage -repl -h` for more details.
To call `your.namespace/your-function` on `arg1` and `arg2`:
The `./bin/mage -repl` command returns three separate, independent outputs:
- `value`: The return value of the last expression (best for data structures)
- `stdout`: Any printed output from `println` etc. (best for messages)
- `stderr`: Any error messages (best for warnings and errors)
```bash
- Use `println` for human-readable messages
- If `CLOJURE_STYLE_GUIDE.adoc` exists in the working directory, also check compliance with the comm
- [ ] Descriptive names (no `tbl`, `zs'`)
- [ ] `kebab-case` for all variables and functions
- [ ] Side-effect functions end with `!`
- [ ] Public vars in `src` or `enterprise/backend/src` have useful docstrings
- [ ] References use `[[other-var]]` not backticks
- [ ] `TODO` comments include author and date: `;; TODO (Name 1/1/25) -- description`
- [ ] Everything `^:private` unless used elsewhere
- [ ] No `declare` when avoidable (public functions near end)
- [ ] No blank lines within definition forms (except pairwise constructs in `let`/`cond`)
- [ ] Separate `deftest` forms for distinct test cases
- [ ] Pure tests marked `^:parallel`
- [ ] Test names end in `-test` or `-test-<number>`
- [ ] Correct module patterns (OSS: `metabase.<module>.*`, EE: `metabase-enterprise.<module>.*`)
- [ ] API endpoints in `<module>.api` namespaces
- [ ] Public API in `<module>.core` with Potemkin
- [ ] No cheating module linters with `:clj-kondo/ignore [:metabase/modules]`
- [ ] Response schemas present (`:- <schema>`)
- [ ] Query params use kebab-case, bodies use `snake_case`
- [ ] Routes use singular nouns (e.g., `/api/dashboard/:id`)
- [ ] `GET` has no side effects (except analytics)
- [ ] No raw MBQL manipulation outside `lib`, `lib-be`, or `query-processor` modules
- [ ] Uses `t2/select-one-fn` instead of selecting full rows for one column
- [ ] New multimethods documented in `docs/developers-guide/driver-changelog.md`
- [ ] Passes `driver` argument to other driver methods (no hardcoded driver names)
- [ ] Minimal logic in `read-column-thunk`
- [ ] Kondo linter suppressions use proper format (not `#_:clj-kondo/ignore` keyword form)
| `calculate-age`, `get-user`                  | Pure functions should be nouns: `age`, `user`
| `update-db`, `save-model`                    | Missing `!` for side effects: `update-db!`, `save-m
| `snake_case_var`                             | Should use kebab-case
| `;; TODO fix this`                           | Missing author/date: `;; TODO (Name 1/1/25) -- desc
| `(defn foo ...)` in namespace used elsewhere | Should be `(defn ^:private foo ...)`
| `/api/dashboards/:id`                        | Use singular: `/api/dashboard/:id`
| Query params with `snake_case`               | Use kebab-case for query params
> This pure function should be named as a noun describing its return value. Consider `user` instead
> This function is only used in this namespace, so it should be marked `^:private`.
> Query parameters should use kebab-case. Change `user_id` to `user-id`.
- Try to organize namespaces to avoid `declare` (put public functions near the end)
- Use Lib and MBQL 5 in new source code; avoid legacy MBQL
> richer feedback, and avoid shell escaping issues. Only use `./bin/mage -repl` as a fallback
- Do not post comments confirming things "look good" or telling them they did something correctly

content.value_statement: Developers need reliable Metabase Clojure reviews that catch project-specific issues before merge. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a focused checklist for diffs and pull requests.
actual_capabilities: Checks Clojure and ClojureScript naming, docstring, visibility, and formatting conventions.
Reviews tests for structure, names, parallel safety, and expected coverage.
Flags Metabase module, REST API, MBQL, Toucan, and driver convention violations.
Guides use of Metabase lint, formatting, readability, test, and REPL commands.
Provides review comment examples focused on concrete style problems.
limitations: Tailored to Metabase conventions and may not fit other Clojure projects.
Requires the reviewer to inspect diffs and local files; it does not parse code automatically.
Some checks depend on Metabase scripts or optional clojure-mcp tools being available.
It should not replace human judgment for architecture, security, or product behavior.

use_cases.title: Review a Metabase pull request
use_cases.description: Check changed Clojure and ClojureScript files for project style, test, API, and module issues before merge.

use_cases.title: Prepare code before review
use_cases.description: Run through the checklist before opening a pull request and fix convention problems early.

use_cases.title: Standardize review feedback
use_cases.description: Keep comments focused on actionable violations instead of praise or broad style opinions.

prompt_templates.title: Review a small diff
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a short Clojure change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Clojure diff with the Metabase Clojure review checklist. Focus on naming, docstrings, tests, and formatting issues.

prompt_templates.title: Check a namespace
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review of one changed namespace.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this changed namespace for Metabase conventions. Check visibility, function size, docstrings, tests, and clear review comments.

prompt_templates.title: Audit API conventions
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of endpoint and module work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this API or module change for Metabase rules. Check route naming, schemas, tests, namespace placement, MBQL usage, and database access.

prompt_templates.title: Run a full review flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced pull request review with local validation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this pull request using the full Metabase Clojure workflow. Use available lint, formatting, readability, test, and REPL checks only when appropriate.

output_examples.input: A pull request adds an API endpoint with plural route naming and no endpoint tests.
output_examples.output: The review flags the route naming issue, asks for endpoint tests, and requests complete parameter and response schemas.

output_examples.input: A namespace adds local helper functions with broad visibility and command-style pure names.
output_examples.output: The review recommends private visibility for local helpers and noun-based names for pure return values.

output_examples.input: A driver change adds a new multimethod but omits documentation updates.
output_examples.output: The review asks for the driver changelog update and checks that implementation passes the driver argument through.

best_practices: Provide the diff and relevant namespace paths so the review can verify context.
Run lint, formatting, and targeted tests before requesting final review.
Ask for actionable comments only, focused on concrete Metabase convention violations.
anti_patterns: Using the skill as a general Clojure style authority outside Metabase projects.
Posting praise or approval comments when no issue needs action.
Running REPL or project commands in an untrusted workspace.

faq.question: Does this skill work outside Metabase?
faq.answer: It can help, but its rules are tailored to Metabase. Other Clojure projects may use different conventions.

faq.question: Can it run tests and linters?
faq.answer: It describes Metabase commands for linting, formatting, readability, tests, and REPL checks. Run them only in trusted workspaces.

faq.question: Does it replace clj-kondo?
faq.answer: No. It uses lint results as review input and focuses on convention gaps that automated tools may miss.

faq.question: Will it comment on clean code?
faq.answer: No. It instructs reviewers to post only actionable issues that need a change.

faq.question: What files should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide changed Clojure or ClojureScript files, related tests, and any relevant style guide context.

faq.question: Does it check security?
faq.answer: Only indirectly through API behavior and review quality rules. Use a security review for threat modeling and secrets.
